item.title: The Inverse of Right-continuous Non-decreasing Function
item.description: The inverse of a right-continuous non-decreasing function appears a lot in probability. I used to have a hard time to remember the precise form of it. Here is a little digging into this problem. The inverse of a right-continuous non-decreasing function can be defined in two ways: \[F^{-1}(w) = \sup\{ y: F(y) \leq w\} \quad \text{or} \quad F^{-1}(w) = \inf\{y: F(y) > w\}\] The inverse of a left-continuous non-decreasing function can be defined in two ways: \[G^{-1}(w) = \sup\{ y: G(y) < w\} \quad \text{or} \quad G^{-1}(w) = \inf\{y: G(y) \geq w\}\]
